change.why_safe: Measurement-only; no engine.py change, so no new safety argument is needed beyond the ones PRs #1173/#1174/#1176 already established (maximal-munch suffix-anchor correctness, unchanged).

reproduction.method: self-contained before/after via a monkeypatched _probe_delta_from_anchor that always returns None (forcing full-prefix relex on every probe), identical technique to PRs #1174/#1176; a swap-in of engine.py at pre-fix commit 20b658f (via git show, restored after) used separately to confirm the new unit tests are not vacuous
reproduction.long_program: Same 10-line, multi-statement valid OpenUI DSL program as PRs #1174/#1176's LONG_PROGRAM, with Slider's first argument changed from the free-form literal "$level" to the placeholder ":slot_level" so DSLNativeTokenizer.encode accepts it.
reproduction.drive_pattern: Exact per-candidate loop shape from compiler_draft.py's build_completion_forest: skip LIT_STR/LIT_NUM/LIT_END marker tokens, probe each remaining token's token_surface_piece against the currently-synced prefix without committing, then commit via advance() on a truthy probe or set_prefix() on a None (fallback) probe.
reproduction.scripts_not_committed: none -- measurement used inline python -c invocations against the committed test module's own helpers (LONG_PROGRAM, _realistic_chunks, _drive_realistic_chunks, _CharCountingEngine, _disabled_anchor), not a separate scratch script

interpretation: Answers PR #1176's open question: at the real call site's realistic chunk granularity, the chars-lexed reduction is far larger (7.29x vs 1.98x) than the char-by-char synthetic drive suggested -- fewer, larger probe calls widen (not narrow) the gap between the full-relex baseline (which re-lexes the entire growing prefix every call) and the suffix-anchor path (anchored to one boundary token regardless of chunk size). Wall-time speedup barely moves (1.56x vs 1.50x) because InteractiveParser.copy()'s fixed per-call cost is a larger fraction of each call's total time with fewer (152 vs 543) calls, diluting the much larger lex-work reduction's relative wall-time benefit.
